chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and life on the road
title: Dizzy and Babs Gonzales rehearsing at her Douglas House apartment
summary: Around 1944 she lived at the Douglas House in New York, and Dizzy Gillespie, Babs Gonzales and others rehearsed and ate at her place. She cooked and told them to clean up after themselves.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: When I lived in New York and I had the apartment and Dizzy and them used to come up there and rehearse at my place, you know?
No, when was that?
That was in New York.
Around when?
Around . . .
Was that after you left Basie?
Yeah.
When you said you had that restaurant,

Yeah, around '44.
You had an apartment there? Where abouts?
Yeah, at the Douglas House.
Oh, alot of people live at the Douglas House, don't they?
Yeah.
Some of the dancers and Honey Coles, and people like that.

Yeah, everybody used to live there. They'd come up to my house and they'd rehearse, you know. When I wasn't working, you know, they'd call me up, "hey Humes, I know you done cooked. what you got to eat up there, we coming up". I said, "no, you got the wrong number. This ain't the restaurant". And they said, "well we coming on up there," and Babs Gonzalez'. I said, "well, you know I got food here".
Well, wouldn't they leave a little change?
Change, what's that? They knew I had cooked. And I'd even have drinks. And then I'd say,

"Now I'm going to bed. Now you can come on and go in there and fix what you want and clean up after yourself, and put the food away". And that's it.
You let them do that?
Yeah, I'd have food all cooked and then I's set the table for them. And then they could go and help themselves to the food.
And would they bring chicks with them or would it be just guys?
Just guys.
